name: Implementation Intentions
description: Forming a specific if-then plan that links an anticipated situational cue to a concrete intended action substantially increases the odds that the action actually gets initiated and completed, compared to holding only a general goal.
design_relevance_note: The rationale behind goal-setting flows that prompt a user to specify when and where they'll act (e.g. a habit or reminder app asking 'when will you do this?' instead of just 'set a goal').
myth_risk_note: The meta-analytic effect size is medium-to-large and the mechanism (cue accessibility, automated responding) is independently supported within the same meta-analysis -- no indication of a popularity/evidence mismatch.
prevalence_note: Standard concept in behavior-change and habit-formation product design, though less universally known outside that niche than e.g. anchoring or scarcity.

findings.description: Meta-analysis of 94 independent tests finds implementation intentions have a medium-to-large positive effect (d = .65) on goal attainment, working by promoting initiation of goal striving, shielding ongoing goal pursuit from unwanted influences, disengagement from failing courses of action, and conservation of capability for future goal striving; support was also found for the proposed mechanisms of heightened cue accessibility and automated goal-directed responding.
findings.source_title: Implementation Intentions and Goal Achievement: A Meta-Analysis of Effects and Processes

findings.description: Reviewing a program of experimental studies, Gollwitzer finds that supplementing a mere goal intention with a specific implementation intention (an if-then plan linking an anticipated situational cue to a concrete goal-directed response) substantially increases the likelihood that people actually initiate and complete the intended action, compared to holding the goal intention alone.
findings.source_title: Implementation Intentions: Strong Effects of Simple Plans

applications.title: PARC Coach: a real mobile health app's if-then planning prompts nearly tripled goal-completion odds
applications.description: PARC Coach, a mobile health app studied by Pirolli et al. (Journal of Medical Internet Research, November 30, 2017), had 64 adult participants pick a behavioral goal (eating more slowly, walking, or eating more vegetables) and then build a concrete implementation intention for it directly in the app: specifying the time of day, location, who they'd be with, and when the behavior would happen, plus how far in advance they wanted a reminder. Over a 28-day field deployment, receiving a reminder tied to that specific plan was associated with substantially higher goal-completion odds than not receiving one (odds ratio 7.52, P<.001), with mean daily success rates of 0.32-0.55 when reminders were used versus 0.18 without them. How recently a reminder had been acknowledged also predicted success independently.
applications.ethical_note: The mechanism helps users follow through on health goals they themselves selected, using their own specified plan rather than an externally imposed one -- a clean, low-risk use of the technique with no persuasion-against-interest dimension.
